package_info.package_versions: N/A (modifies arbitrary native executables on infected systems)
package_info.why_malicious: Azov wiper is considered malicious because it modifies native executable files on affected systems by injecting them with malicious code that irreversibly destroys data. Despite referring to itself as ransomware, it does not offer any decryption or recovery mechanism, making it a destructive wiper rather than a financially motivated ransomware.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into native Windows executable files (.exe, .dll)

malicious_snippets.code_language: C/C++ (native Windows binary code, pseudocode shown)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injected code enumerates files on the system, overwrites their contents with random data, and corrupts file headers, resulting in irreversible data destruction.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is highly suspicious because legitimate software does not inject code into other executables to overwrite unrelated files with random data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal executables do not self-modify or inject destructive code into other binaries, nor do they irreversibly destroy user data without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: File shredding utilities may overwrite files for secure deletion, but only on user-specified targets and with explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Mass file overwriting with random data
No recovery or decryption mechanism provided

attack_chain.action: Initial infection: Azov wiper is delivered to the victim system (vector not specified, but typically via phishing, trojanized software, or exploit).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code injection into native executables

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into native Windows executables on the system.
When an infected executable is launched, the injected Azov wiper code executes, overwriting files and corrupting data.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected code injection into native Windows executables
Mass file overwriting with random or junk data
Destructive file operations without user interaction
No communication for ransom payment or decryption
file_indicators: Native executables (.exe, .dll) with unexpected code sections or altered headers
Files with contents replaced by random data
Absence of ransom notes or decryption instructions
network_indicators: Typically none, as Azov wiper does not communicate for ransom payment or exfiltration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected modifications to native executable files, especially the presence of new or altered code sections. Detect mass file overwriting or corruption events, particularly those that occur without user initiation. Use endpoint protection to identify known Azov wiper signatures and behaviors. Alert on destructive file operations that do not match legitimate file shredding or update patterns.
